ai.title: Move cloud PR delivery cron to graphile runner
ai.summary: The `reconcile_pr_delivery` job in the shared `CONVEX_CRON_JOB_RUNNERS` table is moved from the `convex` runner to the graphile runner. The accompanying doc comment notes that its threads are in Postgres and the Convex cron is deleted, so freebuff-web now runs the body with its own GitHub App key. This is the final entry in the table to flip, making all platform Convex cron jobs run on graphile.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/constants/convex-cron-jobs-runner.ts`, the `CONVEX_CRON_JOB_RUNNERS` table entry for `reconcile_pr_delivery` is changed from `'convex'` to `'graphile'`, and its doc comment is updated to note that its threads are in Postgres and the Convex cron is deleted.

This change only affects the engineers who run the Freebuff service itself and does not alter how you use the assistant, view code, or manage your account. There is no new feature, performance improvement, or visible change for you in daily use.

entries.title: Shared/Core update: billboard
entries.summary: Shared/Core changes across 1 file(s) (+4/−2).

ai.title: Billboard sidebar hourly cap reduced and max show constant added
ai.summary: The hourly impression limit for the Desktop-Billboard-Sidebar ad slot in `common/src/ads/billboard.ts` is reduced from 2 to 1 per rolling hour. This change tightens the frequency cap to prevent a campaign from spending its daily allowance too quickly in a single sitting. A new constant, `BILLBOARD_SIDEBAR_MAX_SHOW_MS`, is also defined to set a maximum lifetime of 3 minutes for a sidebar showing, though it is not yet read by any code in the provided context.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/ads/billboard.ts`, the `BILLBOARD_FREQUENCY_CAPS` hourly limit for `BILLBOARD_SIDEBAR_PLACEMENT_ID` is reduced from 2 to 1, and the new constant `BILLBOARD_SIDEBAR_MAX_SHOW_MS` is exported but has no visible reader in the provided diff or source context.
ai.unknowns: The specific runtime component that will consume the new `BILLBOARD_SIDEBAR_MAX_SHOW_MS` constant is not visible in the diff or provided source context.

eli5.text: The limit on how often an advertiser's image ad can appear in the desktop app's sidebar is now set to once per hour instead of twice. A new rule was also added to cap the total time a sidebar ad can stay on screen at three minutes, though this limit is not yet active in the app. This adjustment affects advertisers buying ad space, ensuring their campaigns do not use up their daily ad budget too quickly in a single burst. Regular users will see slightly fewer repeated ads in the sidebar during an hour, but no other parts of the app change.

entries.title: Shared/Core update: hosted-workspace
entries.summary: Shared/Core changes across 2 file(s) (+155/−52).

ai.title: Sites local bundler names missing relative paths and adds desktop
ai.summary: The local Sites bundler in `common/src/sites/local-files.ts` now distinguishes missing files from containment violations in `localPath`, returning specific 'Site file not found' errors for relative paths inside the workspace while preserving the existing refusal for absolute or external paths. Concurrently, `common/src/desktop-cloud/hosted-workspace.ts` adds `sitesContext` and `sitesPublish` optional methods to the `HostedWorkspaceHost` interface, allowing the desktop app to read local site compatibility and trigger local build streaming for the Publish button. These changes are supported by new tests verifying that relative manifest paths resolve correctly and that missing files are named in error messages without exposing the absolute root.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies `common/src/sites/local-files.ts` to add `outside` and `missing` helpers and rework `localPath` to catch ENOENT/ENOTDIR errors, and modifies `common/src/desktop-cloud/hosted-workspace.ts` to add `sitesContext` and `sitesPublish` methods to `HostedWorkspaceHost`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the native Electron implementation of the new `sitesContext` and `sitesPublish` host methods.

eli5.text: The desktop app now has the setup to let you build and publish websites directly from a chat that is running on your own computer. The process for gathering your local project files was also improved so that if a file is missing, the error message clearly names the specific folder it tried to find it in, rather than giving a generic warning. This affects you if you use the desktop version of the app to manage local projects; for most people, this is internal preparation for a new feature and does not change how your current sessions or free credits work.

ai.title: Clarify CLI Freebucks refund copy with session hold and daily cap
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI updates the user-facing text for Freebucks refund receipts in `cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts` to clarify the mechanics of session retention and daily limits. The `refundPending` state now includes the note that each session keeps one hour of its price, and the zero-refund case explicitly states that refunds never refill a daily allowance that is already used up. These copy adjustments in the `freebucksRefundLine` helper align the CLI's messaging with the server-side rule established on 2026-10-28, reducing user confusion about why early session termination still consumes a full hour.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts`, the docblock for `freebucksRefundLine` and its two user-facing string returns are updated to explicitly mention that a session keeps one hour and that refunds do not refill daily allowances.
ai.unknowns: The diff shows only the CLI-side text changes and does not include the corresponding server-side implementation of the 2026-10-28 one-hour retention rule.

eli5.text: The words displayed in the terminal when a paid credit refund is pending or settled were updated to explain the new billing rules. This affects people who use the command-line version of the coding assistant and have paid compute credits. The text now clearly states that every session reserves one hour of its price and that a refund will not top up a daily limit that has already been used for the day.
